patterns.what_worked: The spec's own template made the build mechanical: copying api.scan_player_aura's loop shape and reusing its 40-row cap kept the generalisation provably identical, and driving the wrapper's real secret guard (issecretvalue) in the pin proved the degrade instead of simulating it. The client-source mirror answered the INVSLOT_* and GetInventoryItemID citations read-only, so no id or slot number was asserted from memory.
patterns.what_was_hard: api.GetInventoryItemID returns nil for three different things (global absent / restricted reading / empty slot), so 'the read is readable' is not directly observable through the mandated read path. Resolved conservatively: one non-nil slot read is the evidence, all-nil answers nil (unknown), never false. Also had to chase a luacheck warning the new pin block introduced (an overwritten 'stacks') to hold the 2-warning floor.
patterns.skill_gap: Tri-state probes need the caller contract spelled out in the code, not just in the bench file: a downstream lane that writes 'probe() or nil' silently loses the false branch. The BS-2 spec line carries exactly that hazard and is flagged in the bench file for the orchestrator.
